That tension has been at its highest concentration with the new blue elves it debuted with WoW: Forever. The Skyborne have never existed in WoW before; they look almost exactly like the Blood Elves from The Burning Crusade expansion, but their lore tells us they're a faction of High Elves. title: Steam is about to start getting some of the best Japanese pixel art in gaming history
summary: It only took about 35 years for these PC-98 games to start being released in English.
body: Japan's NEC PC-98 series of personal computers, popular in the 1980s and 1990s, were home to hundreds of adventure games and visual novels with absolutely impeccable pixel art. It was a whole vibe— sometimes cute , sometimes incredibly detailed with a very limited color palette , and very (very) often pornographic. Very few of these games were ever officially released in English—the whole pornographic thing probably being a big reason why—but better late than never, right? A fan translation group named WINE has released five English translations for PC-98 games in the last three years, including a pair of horror adventures called Dead of the Brain and Dead of the Brain 2. And the first one is now getting an official release on Steam juuuust in time for Halloween, with enhancements like autosaves and "optional quality-of-life improvements such as hover hints and hit boxes." I've played a chunk of Dead of the Brain 2, and can't fully recommend them—they're pretty basic and a bit tedious as adventure games, and in schlocky horror B-movie fashion love to throw in some sexual violence—but damn do I love how these games look. title: World of Warcraft: Forever drops the PvP grind so normal people can have fancy titles too
summary: Blizzard outlines how PvP ranks will work in the throwback MMO.
body: Even though I was way too new (and low level) to understand how PvP worked in World of Warcraft's early days, I knew by osmosis that it was made for tryhards. WoW PvP was not only a massive grind, but a competition against other grinders for a unique title that no normal person would even dare to go for. WoW: Forever borrows a lot from the classic game, but the torturous PvP system won't be one of them. In a new blog post , Blizzard explains how it has simplified the system overall to avoid asking players to derail their entire lives for bragging rights. Those old titles are still there—High Warlord for Horde players and Grand Marshal for Alliance—but you won't be racing to keep your place on an invisible leaderboard every week. Instead, it's going to be pretty straight forward: Anyone who plays a lot of PvP will get rewarded eventually. You'll have a currency and a point-based progression system to worry about. Honor is the currency you'll earn for killing enemy players, completing battlegrounds, and finishing PvP quests. title: أن تموت واقفًا أو تعيش راكضًا.. ميسي ورونالدو طريقان مختلفان للخلود
summary: البقاء والاكتفاء بين ميسي ورونالدو.. أيهما أذكى؟

title: "لم يعطونا شيئًا".. مدرب بنين يشكو سوء معاملة الأرجنتين في ليلة وداع ميسي
summary: "كان الأمر صعبًا للغاية"
body: "كان الأمر صعبًا للغاية" اشتكى جيرنوت روهر، المدير الفني لبنين، من سوء معاملة الأرجنتين، لفريقه خلال زيارته التي شهدت خوض ودية فجر اليوم، شهدت الظهور الأخير ليونيل ميسي. وفاز منتخب "الألبيسيليستي" بنتيجة 3-0، وسط حضور جماهيري كبير، وبينما احتفل الأرجنتينيون بظهور أسطورتهم الأخير، حاول لاعبو بنين تبادل القمصان ومشاركة لحظة مميزة مع الأرجنتينيين، لكن دون جدوى. وأكد المدرب جيرنوت روهر، ذلك في برنامج "Rothen s'enflamme " الإذاعي على محطة "RMC". وقال: " نعم، كان الأمر صعبًا للغاية. لقد حاولنا. العيب الوحيد هو أن الأرجنتينيين لم يعطونا شيئًا. لا صورة لميسي، ولا قميص. حتى أنهم لم يسمحوا لنا بالدخول إلى الممر، ولا حتى إلى غرفة الملابس". ناقش الموضوعات والأخبار بشكل أعمق في منتديات كووورة وتابع: "رفض الأمن دخول الجميع. جاء بعض اللاعبين لتبادل القمصان، لذلك كنا نعلم أن الأمر سيكون صعبًا. جربنا كل شيء، لكننا لم نحصل على شيء". وأكمل المدرب الألماني: "عرضنا باقة من الزهور بألوان بنين - الأصفر والأحمر والأخضر - لكن ذلك لم ينجح. مع ذلك، أعطيت قميص ميسي لعام 2018 للمدرب سكالوني، والذي جعله يوقعه لي ثم أعاده إليّ، لكن هذا كان كل شيء".

body: The grapple hook is a legit game changer Yeeeeeeeeehooooooooooo! Yeah yeah, sure, Arc Raiders is getting some new guns, but the real star of my session was the grapple hook. Embark made an honest-to-god grapple hook: Not the kind that zips you straight to where you aim it (that already exists), but a simulated rope that's quite rare in videogames. The grapple hook is only a green tier gadget, but very versatile. A single hook lets you: Climb straight up to the top of most buildings Swing from rooftop to rooftop like Spider-Man Safely descend from tall buildings Annoy the crap out of flying Arc bots What makes the grapple hook so useful is that it sticks to just about anything . Wherever the hook lands becomes a pivot point that you can either climb toward, descend, or swing against. You can also redeploy the hook midair, without a cooldown or use limit, meaning you can chain swings together. body: A lot of the 3D games I consider touchstones of thoughtful player movement are a decade or more old: Mirror's Edge, of course, Titanfall 2, Dishonored 2, Doom Eternal or ARMA 3. That's by no means a comprehensive list, but these are the games that come to mind when I think about in-game movement that feels incredibly considered. And if ARMA 3 feels out of place in that list, its sim-style tactical physicality is memorable to anyone who plays it even briefly (me). These each set the ceiling high for what you could achieve with their controls, if you were prepared to learn them. Each offered a power fantasy of some kind to be mastered, whether you're wall-running onto a mech or peeking out across a field to line up a perfect shot. In recent years, though, I feel like it's increasingly common to find developers who want to capture granular, basic movements from real life that have no power fantasy element whatsoever. title: PSA: Star Wars Galactic Racer pilots, put some points in resilience before you hit the acid planet
summary: Holidays on Sentinel I are a real downer.
body: The multiplayer tour mode in Galactic Racer lets you upgrade a speeder over the course of six races while other players manically shunt you into the wall on every track. It's a best-of-both-worlds mode that adds a little of the campaign's run-based progression to a multiplayer tournament. But since you only get one race on each planet, you might be blindsided by Sentinel I. Locations in Galactic Racer tend to follow the Star Wars pattern of single-environment worlds—the desert planet, the jungle planet—and good old Sentinel I is apparently the galaxy's planet of burning piss. Veer a little off-track on Sentinel I and you'll hit boiling yellow acid that quickly tanks your ramjet boost. It's a bad time. While it's normally tempting to throw your precious upgrade points into afterburner and ramjet to get your speed as high as possible, and battery if you've got a decent ability you need more energy for, make sure to put some points in resilience before you get to Sentinel 1 so you aren't instantly tanked the screwed you skim over one of its scenic acid rivers.
